places.name: Ansfelden
places.country: Archduchy of Austria (Austrian Empire; today Austria)
places.what: Born in a village near Linz, where his father inherited the schoolmaster’s post in 1823.

places.name: Windhaag
places.country: Archduchy of Austria (Austrian Empire; today Austria)
places.what: Assistant teacher from seventeen to nineteen, on appalling pay, humiliated by his superior.

places.name: Kronstorf an der Enns
places.country: Archduchy of Austria (Austrian Empire; today Austria)
places.what: A happier two years as assistant teacher, studying with Zenetti in Enns; “Bruckner style” began to appear.

places.name: Sankt Florian monastery
places.country: Archduchy of Austria (Austrian Empire; today Austria)
places.what: Teacher and monastery organist; he is buried in its crypt, directly beneath the organ.

places.name: Old Cathedral, Linz
places.country: Archduchy of Austria (Austrian Empire; today Austria)
places.what: Cathedral organist; studied with Sechter, conducted the Frohsinn society and had his seven-part Ave Maria sung here in 1861.

places.name: Munich
places.what: Met Wagner at the premiere of Tristan und Isolde, which he studied extensively from 1863 onwards.

places.name: Vienna Conservatory
places.what: Took over Sechter’s theory post; added a University of Vienna post in 1875; Mahler attended the conservatory.

places.name: Royal Albert Hall and Crystal Palace, London
places.what: Gave six organ recitals on a new Willis organ at the Albert Hall and five at the Crystal Palace.

places.name: Bayreuth
places.what: Showed Wagner his Second and Third symphonies; Wagner chose the D minor Third, which Bruckner dedicated to him.

places.name: Vienna
places.what: Premiere of the 1877 version of the symphony dedicated to Wagner.

places.name: Vienna
places.what: Premiered under Hans Richter to great acclaim, the first Bruckner symphony premiere he did not conduct himself.

places.name: Opera house, Leipzig
places.what: Premiered under Arthur Nikisch with the Gewandhaus Orchestra, bringing Bruckner his greatest success so far.

places.name: Musikverein, Vienna
places.what: Premiered under Hans Richter, in the Musikverein, in the 1890 version dedicated to Emperor Franz Joseph.

places.name: Sankt Florian monastery church
places.country: Archduchy of Austria (Austrian Empire; today Austria)
places.what: Buried in the crypt of the monastery church, directly beneath the organ he loved.

places.name: Vienna
places.what: Died in Vienna aged seventy-two, still teaching; the Emperor had decorated him in July 1886.

recordings.work: Symphony No. 7 in E major, WAB 107
recordings.movement: III. Scherzo — Sehr schnell; Trio — Etwas langsamer

influences.title: Bruckner dedicates his Third Symphony to Wagner
influences.note: A connection with music at a recorded place; the line does not assert travel or a personal meeting.
